title: Method for the detection of powdery mildew in tomato from electrical signalling
author: Matic, Masoero, et al.

steps.title: Prepare substrate and pots
steps.instruction: Mix peat, coconut granules, and volcanic pumice in a 6:2:1 volume ratio; fill 1 L pots with this mixture; add the NPK+microelements slow‑release fertilizer (Vigorplant, Fombio, Italy); place each pot on a 1 L flask containing unsupplemented tap water; prepare six plants per substrate batch.

steps.title: Germinate seeds and transplant
steps.instruction: Sow tomato seeds in plug trays; after 2 weeks germination, transplant seedlings into the prepared 1 L pots.

steps.title: Maintain fungal isolate
steps.instruction: Keep the MB1 isolate of Oidium neolycopersici (On) on tomato cv. Marmande in a greenhouse at 23 °C day, 19 °C night, and 70 % relative humidity.

steps.title: Inoculate plants
steps.instruction: When plants are 1 month old, select three of the six plants for inoculation; spray two primary leaflets of three randomly chosen leaves per plant with 10 µL of conidial suspension (5 × 10⁻⁴ spores · mL⁻¹) prepared from heavily infected sporulating leaves; keep the remaining three plants as non‑inoculated controls; continue cultivation for an additional 22 days.

steps.title: Assess disease visually and by PCR
steps.instruction: Observe inoculated plants at 8, 15, and 22 days post‑inoculation (dpi) to evaluate disease index (DI) as the percentage of leaf area affected, using the same leaflets throughout; extract DNA from symptomatic leaves, amplify the ITS region with ITS4 and ITS5 primers, verify a 595–596 bp PCR product by Sanger sequencing to confirm On; compute a daily disease rate (DR) by linear regression of DI on dpi; repeat the whole experiment twice and average the results.

steps.title: Insert gold electrodes
steps.instruction: Use custom pure‑gold electrodes (0.1 mm diameter, 10 mm length); insert each electrode into the stem of each plant to a depth of 3 mm to reach the conducting bundles; perform insertion one day before signal recording to allow acclimation.

steps.title: Assemble measurement hardware
steps.instruction: Connect each electrode to a shielded multi‑core cable terminated with the gold electrode; attach cables to screw‑terminal connectors of an Agilent 34970A 6½‑digit Digital Multimeter equipped with a 34901A multiplexer module (the multiplexer can host up to three internal scanner modules, each providing 20 two‑wire measurement channels plus 2 control/reference channels); allocate one voltage channel with a separate ground for each electrode and connect the shield to the ground reference to minimise noise; connect a Pt100 platinum resistance thermometer and a photoresistor light sensor to two dedicated channels on a custom stand placed near the plants.

steps.title: Configure instrument parameters
steps.instruction: Set the DMM to auto‑range; set integration time to 200 power‑line cycles; enable the internal pre‑filter low‑pass with a 3 Hz cut‑off frequency.

steps.title: Set up remote control and logging
steps.instruction: Connect the DMM serial (RS‑232) interface to a USB‑to‑serial converter linked to a Raspberry Pi running Debian GNU/Linux 12; ensure the Pi has Wi‑Fi and SSH access; install a bash script that runs at system boot to start the measurement program and restart it if it terminates; the Python measurement program must initialise and configure the DMM, scan all 20 voltage channels plus the thermometer and light sensor, read values continuously, and write timestamped data to a CSV file on internal memory and on a removable USB key; removal of the USB key automatically pauses acquisition, reinsertion resumes it; configure the program to auto‑start on reboot to recover from power loss.

steps.title: Record electrical signals
steps.instruction: Begin continuous voltage recording from all electrodes and environmental sensors for 15 days, covering the period from 5 to 15 dpi when disease symptoms appear; ensure data are stored as described.

steps.title: Validate electrical data
steps.instruction: After recording, correlate the electrical potential differences between infected and control plants with the visual disease index measured at 8, 15, and 22 dpi; note that electrical differences become detectable as early as 1.9 dpi, confirming the method’s early‑detection capability.
